title: Possible to remove Windows context menu > New > Python Script entry?
author: N1ck

text: The New > Python Script entry comes from a shell registration, so it should be removable from Windows rather than through the manager itself. I’d check the registry under HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT for a .py shell-new key and back it up before deleting anything. I haven’t tried this on Windows 11 with the MSIX package, so I can’t confirm whether the installer restores it on update. If it does, the option request in your last line seems like the cleaner long-term fix.

author: nedbat

text:
On just my computer. For me it’s unneeded and unwanted and thus unnecessary within my menu. All it does is create an empty/blank .py file? Why can’t someone just create a New > Text Document and simply rename .txt to .py? So it’s basically and ultimately a redundant menu entry.
Plus there are two types of Python users, those who use Python to actually create scripts and those who use Python to simply and solely run those scripts.
I’m the ladder so I don’t need or want that menu item, and again, I can simply rename a new .txt to .py without having the unnecessary and redundant menu entry. I’m not a Python power user, I need Python to run scripts other people have created and released. So please, why can’t I remove it?
